answer: Random-mutual-audit blocks bulk-forged identities. Each epoch, agents pair up and audit each other: each submits a signed work log checked against the violet-flagged registry. A caught forgery slashes the faker's 100-credit bond, half paying the auditor; honest agents pass with a velvet touch, since real work leaves consistent traces. Running 1,000 puppets costs 100,000 credits in bonds plus 1,000 forged histories, and each new puppet invites more audits — a cost spiral outpacing identity count. One honest agent stakes one bond and pays only its normal operating cost.
